description: Start turn-by-turn guidance that MapMap runs for you: for a client that can post its position but runs no navigation engine of its own (a voice assistant, glasses, a wearable, a robot, an agent relaying a phone's location). Pass `origin` and `destination`, each `{lat, lon}` or `{place_id}` (a `geocode` id), optional `costing` ("auto" default, "truck", "bus", "motorcycle", "motor_scooter", "bicycle", "pedestrian"), a `truck` profile with costing "truck" (dimensions and the ADR declaration, as on `route`), `landmarks: true` for turns phrased against recognisable places, `language` (e.g. "en-GB") and `units` ("kilometers" or "miles", for the engine's own text; every number here is metres and seconds). To end at a building's door rather than its middle, pass `arrive_at`: "entrance" (the best door of the place at the destination) or `{place_id?, entrance_kind?, wheelchair?}` as on `route` ("point", the default, ends at the destination as given); only doors mapped in OpenStreetMap are chosen, none is estimated, the answer's `arrival` names the door or says `applied: false` with the reason (the session then ends at the destination as given), and every reroute heads for the same door. Returns a `session_id`, the `route` summary, the `first_instruction` to read out, `expires_at` and `privacy`. Then call `check_navigation_progress` with each new position and `end_navigation` on arrival. A SESSION LIVES IN THE GATEWAY'S MEMORY ONLY: it ends after 2 hours with no progress call, when `end_navigation` is called, and whenever the gateway restarts, so a session that has gone is answered by starting a new one from where the traveller is now (`lifetime` says so on every answer). The session keeps the route and the last accepted position only: no trail, nothing written to disk or logs. Guidance is the same engine the MapMap mobile SDKs run on the device; an app with an SDK should navigate on the device instead. Each account holds a limited number of live sessions; without your own key the hosted endpoint holds every keyless caller's sessions on one shared account, so end sessions you are done with. Requires the MapMap gateway (GATEWAY_URL + GATEWAY_API_KEY); see /docs/navigation-sessions.

anyOf.description:
`"entrance"`: end at the best mapped door of the place at the
destination coordinate (the one place with mapped doors within
25 m of it).

`{place_id, entrance_kind, wheelchair}`: end at a door of this
place.

ArriveAt.description:
Where a `route` (or a navigation session, `start_navigation`) should
end at a place: `"entrance"`, or an object naming the place and the
door wanted.

entrance_kind.description:
Only doors of this OpenStreetMap kind: `main`, `yes`, `entry`,
`service`, `staircase`, `home` or `garage`.

place_id.description:
The place whose door to end at (a place result's `id`). Without it
the place is looked up at the destination coordinate.

wheelchair.description:
Step-free access wanted: a door mapped `wheelchair=yes` where one
is mapped, never one mapped `wheelchair=no`.

oneOf.description: End at the place's best mapped door.

EntranceKindWanted.description:
A door kind a route may end at (the ways in; an emergency exit or an
exit-only door is never a destination).

anyOf.description:
A mapped door of the place at the destination, exactly as on
`route`.

NavArriveAt.description:
Where a navigation session ends: `"point"` (the default), or any
`arrive_at` `route` takes (`"entrance"`, or
`{place_id?, entrance_kind?, wheelchair?}`).

oneOf.description: End at the destination's own coordinates.
Lorry; pass a `truck` profile for its dimensions and ADR load.

NavUnits.description: Units the engine's own instruction text uses.

NavWaypoint.description:
Where a navigation session starts or ends: `lat` and `lon`, or a
`place_id`, never both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (−90 to 90). With `lon`.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (−180 to 180). With `lat`.

place_id.description:
A place id from `geocode` (its `id`, returned with
`include_entrances: true`), instead of `lat` and `lon`.

TruckSpec.description:
Truck profile for routing: physical dimensions plus the ADR
dangerous-goods declaration. Omitted dimensions default to the EU
maximum authorised dimensions of Council Directive 96/53/EC (4.0 m
height, 2.55 m width, 16.5 m length, 40 t gross weight).

gross_weight_t.description: Gross combination weight in metric tonnes.

hazmat.description:
Whether the vehicle carries dangerous goods (ADR). Defaults to
false.

tunnel_code.description:
ADR 8.6.4 tunnel restriction code of the load, e.g. "B", "C5000D",
"B/D", or "(-)"/"none" for explicitly unrestricted. Leave unset if
unknown: a hazmat load without a code is conservatively treated as
code B (allowed only through category-A tunnels).

arrive_at.description:
Where the session ends: "point" (default, the destination's own
coordinates), "entrance" (the best door of the place at the
destination), or `{place_id?, entrance_kind?, wheelchair?}`, exactly
as on `route`. A destination given by `place_id` names the place.
Only doors mapped in OpenStreetMap are chosen, none is estimated;
with no door that suits, `arrival` is `applied: false` with the
reason and the session ends at the destination as given. Every
reroute heads for the same door.

landmarks.description:
Landmark phrasing on turns ("Turn right just after the Shell
garage"), on the first route and every reroute. Default false.

origin.description: Where the journey starts: usually where the traveller is now.

truck.description:
Truck profile (dimensions and ADR declaration), as on `route`.
Requires costing "truck".

units.description:
"kilometers" (default) or "miles", for the engine's own instruction
text. Every number this tool returns is in metres and seconds.

name: start_navigation

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

NavInstruction.description: One turn instruction of a navigation session.

direction.description:
Where it is from the traveller ("directly ahead, about 310
metres"), when the fix carried a heading. Read this out rather
than coordinates.

landmark.description:
Landmark phrasing ("Turn left just after the Co-op."), when
landmarks were asked for and one is recognisable there. Prefer it
when reading aloud.

step_index.description: Which step of the route this is.

text.description: The written instruction, e.g. "Turn left onto East Road."

verbal.description: The engine's spoken form, when it has one.

NavRouteSummary.description: The route a navigation session is guiding along.

duration_s.description:
Travel time, seconds. On GB routes this includes the typical-delay
calibration described in `eta_calibration`.

eta_calibration.description:
The GB typical-delay calibration added to the travel time, the same
block as the `route` tool's: `applied`, `method`, `period`,
`engine_time_s`, `added_s`, `alternates_added_s`, `bands`,
`traffic_network_m`, `note`, `sources` and, on trucks, `truck_note`.
Absent when nothing was added.

geometry_polyline6.description: Route geometry, Google encoded polyline with six decimals.

steps.description: How many steps the route has.

version.description: 0 for the first route, one more for every reroute.

PlaceEntrance.description:
One door of a place, as the gateway's `include=entrances` and
`GET /v1/places/{id}/entrances` list it.

Every door served today is a node mapped in OpenStreetMap and tied to
the place on evidence (`source: "osm"`); none is estimated. An empty
list of these means no door is tied to the place, never that the place
has no entrance.

basis.description:
What tied the door to the place: `own_outline`, `stop_area`,
`address_match` or `sole_occupant`.

confidence.description:
How sure the tie between this door and the place is: `high`,
`medium` or `low`. It grades the association, not the door.

ref.description: `ref` as mapped (a station exit number, a door letter).

source.description:
`osm` for a door mapped in OpenStreetMap. `estimated` is reserved
for a door MapMap would infer; none is served today.

wheelchair.description:
`wheelchair=*` as mapped (`yes`, `limited`, `no`, ...); absent when
the map does not say, which is not the same as step-free.

RouteArrival.description: What `route` did about `arrive_at`: the gateway's `arrival` block.

applied.description:
True when the destination was moved to a door. False leaves the
destination where it was given, with the `reason`; the route is
never refused for it.

eligible_entrances.description:
How many of the place's doors suited the costing and the request,
when a door was chosen.

entrance.description: The door the route now ends at.

entrances_index.description:
Whether the deployment's entrance index is `loaded`,
`not-configured` or `failed`.

mapped_entrances.description: How many doors are tied to the place, when a door was chosen.

moved_m.description: How far the destination moved, metres.

original_destination.description: Where the destination was before it moved.

place_id.description: The place whose door was looked for.

reason.description: Why this door, or why no door.

adr.description: The ADR profile applied, when a hazmat truck profile was given.

adr_tunnel_enforcement.description:
What the route does and does not prove about ADR tunnels, when an
ADR profile was given. Relay its caveat.

arrival.description:
Which door the session ends at and why, exactly as `route` reports
it: present when `arrive_at` asked for an entrance. `applied: false`
keeps the destination as given and says why; relay the reason.
Every reroute heads for the same door.

costing.description: The costing the session routes with.

expires_at.description: When the session expires if nothing touches it (RFC 3339, UTC).

idle_ttl_s.description: Idle seconds before expiry; every progress call resets it.

landmarks.description: Landmark summary, when landmarks were asked for.

lifetime.description: How long the session lives and what to do when it is gone.

privacy.description: What the session keeps about the traveller.

session_id.description:
The session id (`nav_` and 32 hex digits). Pass it to
`check_navigation_progress` and `end_navigation`.
